title: Training Note: Waiver-Loss Adjustment on a Reinstated Security Deposit
content:
When a Security Deposits waiver ends and the deposit is reinstated on the waiver reinstatement basis, the reinstatement multiple carries a waiver-loss adjustment that reflects which account's nonpayment disconnection ended the waiver.

## The rule

The waiver-loss adjustment is the qualifying-cut relief of **-0.10** (the multiple is lowered by 0.10) when the reinstated account is not itself disconnected for nonpayment and the account its waiver rested on is disconnected for nonpayment; it is the own-cut surcharge of **0.25** (the multiple is raised by 0.25) when the reinstated account is itself disconnected for nonpayment; and it is nothing otherwise. The adjustment is added to the reinstatement multiple, so the negative qualifying-cut relief lowers it. The reinstatement multiple is never below **1.0**; that floor is applied once, to the multiple as finally reckoned.

Both statuses are read from the Electric Service by Rate Schedule accounts. The account the waiver rested on is the account whose account number is the waiver reference of the waived record.

## Questions answered

**The reinstated account is active; the other account whose history earned the waiver is disconnected for nonpayment. What adjustment?**
-0.10, the qualifying-cut relief.

**The reinstated account is itself disconnected for nonpayment, and the account its waiver rested on is too.**
0.25, the own-cut surcharge: the reinstated account's own disconnection decides it.

**The reinstated account is disconnected for nonpayment and its waiver rested on no other account.**
0.25, the own-cut surcharge.

**Neither account is disconnected for nonpayment.**
No adjustment.

| Reinstated account disconnected for nonpayment | Account the waiver rested on disconnected for nonpayment | Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| no | yes | -0.10 |
| yes | yes or no | 0.25 |
| no | no, or no such account | nothing |
